# An N-slot topology commit restores N documents and one view: no consumer has a sibling projection to converge

## Context

Successor to #18252 / PR #18253, opened at cross-lab review request (@neo-gpt-emmy, RA-1). #18253 delivers the model-atomic seams and they work: `adoptAll` writes every slot or none. What it cannot deliver is the **visible** half, and the reason is structural rather than an omitted callback.

## The measurement

`TopologySeams.commitDockTopologyDocuments` calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange` for the **primary only**. Every sibling slot is written and never projected.

That is not a missing line. Sweeping **every** `workspaceSet.register` call site in the repository:

| site | writer |
|---|---|
| `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:545` (primary) | `document => me.dockModel = document` |
| `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:1757` (vessel) | `document => targetState.document = document` |
| `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs:525/530/535` | `me.dockModel` / `me.popupDocument` / `me.popup2Document` |
| `…:1170/1176` (lazy) | same |
| `test/…/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs:106` | same |

**All seven writers are plain assignments. No registration anywhere supplies a projection**, and the `register` contract is documented `{getDocument, setDocument}` — there is no seam to call.

Two facts make it structural:

1. **`dockModel` is not a reactive config.** No `dockModel_`, no `afterSetDockModel`. Nothing projects off the write — which is exactly why the primary needs its explicit `onDockZoneDocumentChange`. `Workspace`'s own class docblock states the invariant: *"the committed document advances ONLY inside `onDockZoneDocumentChange`."*
2. **A vessel has no projection to converge.** `targetState.document` is written in five places and read only by its own `getDocument`. No component, no renderer, no path.

So a topology restore currently produces **N correct documents and one correct view**. The second window's model is right and its screen is stale.

## Why it is not #18253's scope

Fixing this needs both a projection seam on the `register` contract *and* a vessel-side projection for it to call. The second does not exist in any consumer, and building it is the popup/document-ownership question live on **D#18224** — Options G and H both turn on who owns a vessel's document and who renders from it. Importing that unresolved fork into a seams PR would decide it by implementation accident.

Reviewer agreed: *"Do NOT import D#18224's unresolved ownership fork into #18253."*

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceSet#register` contract | D#18224 → #18303 (ownership resolved: G/H settled) | states explicitly whether it carries projection, or that projection is the host's and the seam is document-only | neither stated ⇒ today's ambiguity, which let an N-slot commit look complete | `WorkspaceSet` class docblock | the seven registration sites; `TopologySeams#onDockZoneDocumentChange` is primary-only, bound stated in-comment |
| every-live-workspace presentation | #18252 (the arm this was written to protect) | a topology restore converges **every** live workspace projection, not only the primary | primary-only ⇒ the sibling window stays stale and green | seam docblock | a second workspace changed away from capture, restored, then **presents** the restored tree |
| the witness host | AC-2 | production-shaped host, not a plain data holder | a projecting fixture proves something no consumer does | spec docblock | current fixture's writers are plain assignments *because production's are too* |
| fail / compensation | ADR 0029 §2.8.3 (post-commit render-target effects) | a failed sibling projection is surfaced, not swallowed; the commit's document truth is unaffected | silent ⇒ the exact failure mode of the primary-only path | seam docblock | mutation arm: removing the sibling projection **reds** the arm |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A topology restore converges **every live workspace projection**, not only the primary. Witnessed by a second workspace that has changed away from the capture, is restored, and then **presents** the restored tree — not by asserting its document.
- [ ] The witness uses a **production-shaped host**, not a plain data holder. The current fixture's writers are plain assignments *because production's are too*; a fixture that projects would prove something no consumer does.
- [ ] Whatever carries the projection is reachable from the `register` contract, or the contract states that projection is the host's responsibility and the seam is document-only. **Either is acceptable; leaving it ambiguous is not** — today's ambiguity is what let an N-slot commit look complete.
- [ ] Mutation-verified: removing the sibling projection reds the arm. An arm that passes while the second window stays stale is the exact failure #18252 was written to prevent.

## Part of

**#18303** — the D#18224 graduation Epic (transactions, topology, reload). The popup/topology ownership decision that gated this ticket is **resolved** there; native blockers are set on the Epic graph, so this section no longer carries the dependency in prose.
